demographics: Most common form of uveitis, accounting for roughly half of all uveitis cases
Often associated with HLA-B27-related spondyloarthropathies in young adults
In children, more often associated with juvenile idiopathic arthritis and usually asymptomatic

risk_factors.text: Herpes simplex or varicella-zoster ocular infection

comorbidities: Inflammatory bowel disease (Crohn disease, ulcerative colitis)

chief_complaints.text: My eye is red and really hurts
My eye feels like it's watering all the time

hpi.onset: Subacute, developing over hours to a few days
hpi.duration: Days to a few weeks at presentation if untreated
hpi.progression: Pain and redness build over one to several days; vision may worsen as inflammation and cells accumulate in the anterior chamber
hpi.location: One eye, typically; can be bilateral in systemic disease
hpi.radiation: Pain may radiate to the brow or temple on the affected side
hpi.quality: Deep, aching, boring pain; often described as a dull ache in or around the eye
hpi.timing: Constant, worse with light exposure and with near work

associated_symptoms.text: Redness around the colored part of the eye
Small pupil that does not dilate well
Sensitivity to light in the unaffected eye when a light is shone in the affected eye

pertinent_negatives: Severe deep eye pain with nausea and vomiting

positives.text: Scaly rash on elbows or knees

atypical.how_it_differs: Children, especially those with juvenile idiopathic arthritis, often have a quiet, white eye with no pain or redness; the inflammation is found only on screening slit-lamp examination.
More likely to be associated with herpes zoster ophthalmicus or masquerade syndromes; pain may be less prominent and vision loss more prominent.
Higher risk of infectious causes such as cytomegalovirus or herpes simplex, often with less pain and more indolent course.
Presentation is similar, but treatment options are limited; topical corticosteroids are generally safe, and systemic immunosuppression requires obstetric input.

general.mild: Alert, uncomfortable, squinting on the affected side; prefers dim light
general.moderate: Ill at ease, keeps the affected eye closed or shaded, tears running down the cheek
general.severe: Distressed, avoids light, guards the eye, reluctant to open it
general.critical: Not typical for isolated anterior uveitis; if present, consider a masquerade syndrome or another cause of the red eye

labs.caveat: Nonspecific; may be normal in isolated HLA-B27-associated anterior uveitis and elevated when there is an underlying systemic inflammatory disease.
Supports an underlying systemic inflammatory process; normal does not exclude uveitis.
Leukocytosis is not typical of isolated anterior uveitis; consider an infectious or systemic cause when present.

findings.text: Upper lobe infiltrates or cavitation suggesting tuberculosis

imaging.preferred_when: Chest x-ray abnormal or sarcoidosis strongly suspected

findings.text: Perilymphatic nodules along fissures and bronchovascular bundles
Ground-glass or fibrotic change in advanced disease

imaging.study: MRI brain and orbits with and without contrast
imaging.preferred_when: Suspected multiple sclerosis or optic nerve involvement

findings.text: Periventricular or juxtacortical T2 hyperintense white matter lesions
Optic nerve enhancement or T2 hyperintensity

imaging.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast

findings.text: Bowel wall thickening with mural enhancement
Mesenteric fat stranding or creeping fat
Fistula, abscess, or stricture in complicated Crohn disease

imaging.preferred_when: Inflammatory back pain with normal radiographs

findings.text: Bone marrow edema at the sacroiliac joints (active sacroiliitis)
Erosions or ankylosis in chronic disease

imaging.preferred_when: Atypical or recurrent uveitis, or suspected retinal or vascular involvement

findings.text: Optic disc leakage or macular edema

decision_points: Anterior uveitis is a clinical diagnosis made on slit-lamp examination; do not delay treatment while waiting for laboratory results
Order HLA-B27 and inflammatory markers in a young adult with acute unilateral uveitis and features of a spondyloarthropathy
Order chest imaging and ACE when uveitis is bilateral or granulomatous, or when sarcoidosis is suspected
Screen for syphilis and HIV in atypical, bilateral, or recurrent uveitis
Check for tuberculosis before starting systemic immunosuppression
In children, screen for juvenile idiopathic arthritis-associated uveitis even when the eye is white and quiet

severity.mild: Mild anterior chamber inflammation with eye pain and redness, preserved visual acuity, normal intraocular pressure, and no posterior synechiae
severity.moderate: Marked anterior chamber cells and flare with blurred vision, photophobia, and mild reduction in visual acuity but no hypopyon or synechiae
severity.severe: Dense anterior chamber inflammation with hypopyon, posterior synechiae, raised intraocular pressure, or markedly reduced visual acuity
severity.critical: Not typical for isolated anterior uveitis; a critically ill presentation should prompt consideration of a masquerade syndrome such as endophthalmitis, a systemic vasculitis, or another cause of the red eye

red_flags.finding: Severe pain with nausea and vomiting and halos around lights
red_flags.meaning: Suggests acute angle-closure glaucoma with markedly elevated intraocular pressure; needs urgent ophthalmology evaluation

red_flags.finding: Recent intraocular surgery or intravitreal injection with rapidly worsening vision
red_flags.meaning: Suggests endophthalmitis; requires urgent vitreous tap and intravitreal antibiotics
Dense anterior chamber inflammation; consider Behçet disease, HLA-B27-associated disease, or an infectious cause such as endophthalmitis

red_flags.finding: Markedly reduced visual acuity or a new visual field defect
red_flags.meaning: Suggests macular involvement, severe inflammation, or another diagnosis such as retinal detachment or optic neuritis

red_flags.finding: Flashes of light or a curtain over the vision
red_flags.meaning: Suggests retinal detachment; needs urgent dilated fundus examination

red_flags.finding: Bilateral or granulomatous uveitis with systemic symptoms
red_flags.meaning: Suggests sarcoidosis, syphilis, tuberculosis, or another systemic cause requiring a broader workup

complications.name: Posterior synechiae
clues: Adhesions between the iris and anterior lens capsule on slit-lamp examination

complications.name: Secondary glaucoma
clues: Optic disc cupping on fundus examination

complications.name: Cataract
clues: History of recurrent or chronic uveitis

complications.name: Macular edema
clues: Macular thickening on optical coherence tomography

complications.name: Band keratopathy
clues: Calcium deposits in the superficial cornea on slit-lamp examination
Chronic inflammation, especially in children with juvenile idiopathic arthritis

special_populations.differences: Often associated with juvenile idiopathic arthritis and presents with a white, quiet eye without pain or redness; diagnosis depends on screening slit-lamp examination, and complications such as band keratopathy and cataract are more common.
More likely to be associated with herpes zoster ophthalmicus or a masquerade syndrome; pain may be less prominent and vision loss more prominent.
Higher risk of infectious causes such as cytomegalovirus or herpes simplex, often with less pain and a more indolent course; a lower threshold for infectious workup and vitreous sampling.
Presentation is similar; topical corticosteroids are generally considered safe, but systemic immunosuppression requires obstetric input and avoidance of teratogenic agents such as methotrexate.

key_questions.question: When did the eye pain and redness start, and how quickly did they develop?
key_questions.looking_for: Subacute onset over hours to a few days; sudden onset over minutes suggests acute angle-closure glaucoma

key_questions.question: Is the pain deep and aching, and does it radiate to the brow or temple?
key_questions.looking_for: Deep, boring pain radiating to the brow or temple, typical of anterior uveitis and scleritis

key_questions.question: Does light bother the eye, and does shining a light in the other eye cause pain in the affected eye?
key_questions.looking_for: Photophobia and consensual photophobia, which point to intraocular inflammation

key_questions.question: Is your vision blurry or reduced?
key_questions.looking_for: Mild to moderate blurring; sudden severe visual loss suggests another diagnosis

key_questions.question: Is there any discharge, itching, or foreign body sensation?
key_questions.looking_for: Absent or minimal; purulent discharge suggests bacterial conjunctivitis or keratitis, itching suggests allergy

key_questions.question: Have you had eye trauma, eye surgery, or do you wear contact lenses?
key_questions.looking_for: Recent surgery or injection suggests endophthalmitis; contact lens wear or trauma suggests keratitis

key_questions.question: Have you had an episode like this before?
key_questions.looking_for: Recurrent episodes suggest HLA-B27-associated disease or another systemic cause

key_questions.question: Do you have low back pain or morning stiffness that improves with activity?
key_questions.looking_for: Inflammatory back pain suggesting ankylosing spondylitis or another spondyloarthropathy

key_questions.question: Have you had chronic diarrhea, abdominal pain, or blood in the stool?
Have you noticed a scaly rash on your elbows, knees, or scalp, or nail changes?
Have you had oral or genital ulcers?
Do you have any numbness, tingling, weakness, or double vision?
Is there a family history of ankylosing spondylitis, psoriasis, or inflammatory bowel disease?
key_questions.looking_for: A family history supporting an HLA-B27-associated or autoimmune condition

key_questions.question: Are you taking any medications, including rifabutin, cidofovir, bisphosphonates, or topical prostaglandin drops?
Do you have severe pain with nausea or vomiting, or see halos around lights?
key_questions.looking_for: Acute angle-closure glaucoma, which needs urgent ophthalmology evaluation

key_questions.question: Have you noticed flashes of light, a shower of new floaters, or a curtain over your vision?
key_questions.looking_for: Retinal detachment, which needs urgent dilated fundus examination

reasoning_points: Subacute onset of a painful red eye with photophobia and blurred vision in one eye
Deep, aching eye pain that worsens with light and near work, sometimes radiating to the brow
Ciliary injection concentrated around the limbus rather than diffuse conjunctival redness
Slit-lamp examination showing cells and flare in the anterior chamber, the defining finding
Absence of purulent discharge, itching, and corneal epithelial defect
Consideration of systemic associations such as HLA-B27-related spondyloarthropathies, inflammatory bowel disease, psoriasis, Behçet disease, and sarcoidosis
Exclusion of sight-threatening look-alikes such as acute angle-closure glaucoma, bacterial keratitis, endophthalmitis, and retinal detachment
Recognition that children with juvenile idiopathic arthritis may have a white, quiet eye and require screening slit-lamp examination

easy: Young adult with acute unilateral painful red eye
Slit-lamp cells and flare in the anterior chamber
Known HLA-B27 positivity or ankylosing spondylitis
medium: Recurrent unilateral episodes in a patient with inflammatory back pain
Mild blurring with a small, poorly dilating pupil and posterior synechiae
Raised intraocular pressure without the severe pain and halos of angle-closure glaucoma
Bilateral or granulomatous uveitis prompting a workup for sarcoidosis or syphilis
hard: Child with juvenile idiopathic arthritis and a white, quiet eye found only on screening slit-lamp examination
Older adult with herpes zoster ophthalmicus and less prominent pain but more vision loss
Immunocompromised patient with an indolent, less painful presentation suggesting cytomegalovirus or herpes simplex
Hypopyon with severe inflammation raising concern for Behçet disease or endophthalmitis
Presentation overlapping with scleritis, where the anterior chamber is quiet but the pain is severe and boring
